To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CO2-enrichment conditions during in-vitro photoautotrophic culture of rubber tree plantlet can induce genotypic dependent responses to regulate plant growth, development and adaptation of ex vitro environments.
in vitro photoautrotrophic acclimatized rubber tree plantlets under ambient CO2 condition are more suitable for ex vitro transplantation than those under CO 2-enriched CO 2 condition.

the in vitro photoautotropic system can be used for the acclimatization and ex vitro adaptation process of rubber tree plantlet and the CO2-enrichment condition in photoautotrophic culture system can be used to improve the acclimatized and ex vitro adapted rubber tree plantlets.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the acclimatization and ex vitro adaptation processes of rubber tree plant in response to CO 2-enriched environment and thus, provides an insight into the physiological and biochemical responses of the plantlets to CO2-enrichments in in vitro photoautrotrophic conditions.
the effect of in vitro photo-autotrophic acclimation of rubber tree plantlet in response to CO-enrichment and its subsequent ex vitro performance in acclimatized and ex vitro adapted plantlets.
the acclimatization and ex vitro adaptation in response to CO 2-enriched in vitro conditions in two rubber tree cultivars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the in vitro photoautotropic acclimatization under CO2 enriched conditions was not beneficial for ex vitro adaptation of the plantlets of rubber tree.
in vitro photoautotropic system can be used for in vitro acclimation of rubber tree plantlet under ambient CO2 and CO2-environmental conditions.
the in vitro acclimate plantlets of rubber tree under CO2-en-riched conditions were not able to adapt to the ex vitro environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in vitro photoautotropic acclimatization and direct transplantation of rubber tree plantlet is an effective approach for rubber tree micropropagation.
CO2-enrichment in the in vitro acclamation system of rubber tree plantlet could be a promising tool to enhance the plantlets’ survival and ex vitro adaptation.
in vitro acclimation under CO2-enhanced condition is not suitable for rubber tree cultivar ‘RRIM600’, but it is suitable for rubber tree cv. ‘RRTI413’.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the acclimatization and adaptation of rubber tree plantlet under elevated CO2 conditions is cultivar-specific and can be used as a potential tool in the development of rubber tree plant for ex vitro environments.

the in vitro acclimate plantlets can be directly transplanted to the soil without the need for an ex vitro adaptation process, which is a time and cost effective method for rubber tree micropropagation.
the in vitro acclimate rubber tree plantlets under ambient CO2 can be successfully transplanted into the soil without the loss of plant vigor.
